_comment: Japanese overrides — forces the final Japanese value regardless of what the translate pipeline returns. Every key is pinned as of v1.30.1: the whole message set was rewritten by hand in zh/en, and this machine has no TRANSLATE_API_KEY, so the Japanese was written by hand too rather than generated. Pinning all of it keeps `npm run translate:hooks` from quietly replacing hand-checked wording on whichever machine next has a key. Status lights, set by what actually happened rather than by how alarming it sounds: 🟢 OwnMind did its job (it stopped the AI, it flagged the reply, it checked) — a block is a green light, because blocking is the product working; 🟡 still working but with less protection than usual, or something the reader should look at; 🔴 it did not run, did not check, or is misconfigured. Set by Vin, 2026-08-15, replacing an undifferentiated ⚠️ on every notice — which made a successful block and a total failure look identical.
_comment_meaning: Every notice that reports a check did NOT happen carries an explicit negation attached to the check (…していません / …できず), and every notice that reports one DID ends affirmative. That is not style. In v1.26.174 the pipeline turned zh's bracketed negation 「沒有」被檢查 into the noun 「なし」 and left the predicate affirmative, so gate.failopen told a Japanese reader the command HAD been checked while en.json said it had NOT — on a machine that gets Japanese from its OS locale with no opt-in. tests/hook-locales-ja-meaning.test.js fails if any of these stops denying what the English denies.
_comment_review: Not yet read by a native speaker. The meanings are pinned by test; the naturalness is not.
